title: Call parameter authoring guide and validator feedback loop
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: Define a pragmatic JSON schema authoring format for tool/function calls and implement a validator/feedback loop that produces actionable, human-friendly errors. Goal is to reduce authoring mistakes, enable graceful compatibility with legacy tool manifests, and provide runtime hints to the serving layer for better fallbacks and telemetry.

Motivation: Engineers and partners keep publishing small variations of call parameter schemas (optional fields described inconsistently, union-like shapes expressed as freeform objects). This causes noisy validation errors, poor UX when tools are called, and brittle client-side code. We need a compact authoring surface + runtime validator that: (1) emits clear remediation messages for authors; (2) supports backward-compatible relaxations at runtime; (3) surfaces helpful telemetry for model prompting and routing decisions.

Scope: This ticket covers the authored schema DSL (JSON-friendly conventions), the server-side validator that returns humanized errors, client-visible error codes and suggested fixes, and a gradual rollout plan (opt-in strict mode, migration linting). It does NOT include SDK auto-fixers (tracked separately).

Key design tenets: compactness (authors prefer short manifests), explicitness (optional vs required must be clear), recoverability (server should offer suggested coercions when safe), compatibility (legacy manifests should be supported by a permissive compatibility layer), and debuggability (errors must map to concrete lines/fields in the manifest and to example requests).

Schema authoring conventions (high level):
- Use 'type' to declare primitive types: 'string', 'integer', 'float', 'boolean', 'object', 'array'.
- Use 'required': [ 'fieldA', 'fieldB' ] to list required top-level fields.
- For objects, authors may define 'properties' with short descriptions; we encourage a one-line 'description' per property.
- Support a small set of 'profiles' to express common shapes: 'id-ref', 'text-block', 'kv-list'. Profiles map to canonical runtime validators and telemetry buckets.
- Allow a 'compat' block with 'relaxations' that explicitly records known relaxations for older consumers, e.g. 'accept_null_for_string': true.

Validation behavior:
- Author-time linter: runs at manifest upload and surfaces warnings for deprecated/ambiguous constructs. Warnings do not block deployment.
- Strict deploy-time validator: can be toggled per-project; rejects manifests with incompatible shapes when enabled.
- Runtime validator: when a call arrives, the runtime validates parameters. On failure the runtime returns a structured error with machine codes, a short human message, and suggested remediation steps.

Error taxonomy (high level):
- E_PARAM_MISSING: required field missing. Message shows the field path and examples.
- E_TYPE_MISMATCH: provided type differs from declared type. Includes coercion suggestions (e.g., 'you provided "123" for age; consider converting to integer').
- E_EXTRA_FIELDS: request contained unexpected fields; message includes allowed list and a hint that unknown fields are ignored in permissive mode.
- E_SCHEMA_AMBIGUOUS: authoring-level warning when field definition is underspecified (e.g., union expressed via examples instead of types).
- E_COMPAT_RELAXATION: runtime accepted a request only because a compat relaxation matched; message includes which relaxation and recommends author update.

Human-friendly error format (server response fields):
- code: machine-code (see taxonomy).
- message: one-line summary for users.
- field_path: dot-delimited path to offending field (if applicable).
- example_fix: one or two suggested fixes in plain English.
- docs_link: direct link to the authoring guide section for the specific error.
- telemetry_tag: short tag for metrics aggregation (e.g., 'param.type_mismatch.age').
(We will return these as JSON in the API error envelope.)

Compatibility layer rules:
- Prioritize explicit relaxations declared in 'compat' block in the manifest. If absent, consult historical compatibility heuristics (e.g., allow empty-string -> null coercion for legacy clients).
- Emit E_COMPAT_RELAXATION telemetry whenever a relaxation is applied. These events feed migration dashboards to prioritize manifest updates.
- After a defined deprecation window (configurable per project), warn authors during linting that a relaxation will be removed.

Telemetry & observability:
- Track counts of each error code, latency delta caused by validation, and per-model/per-tool aggregation.
- Surface top offending manifests and example failing payloads (redacted) in Console.
- Add tracing spans around validation steps so we can measure CPU cost and optimize hot paths.

Acceptance criteria (must-haves):
- Authoring DSL documented with examples and a published JSON Schema example in Confluence.
- Server-side validator implemented and wired to runtime call path. When invoked with a known-bad payload it returns one of the defined machine codes and clear remediation text.
- Linter provides warnings for ambiguous authoring patterns and links to docs.
- Compatibility layer honors per-manifest relaxations and emits E_COMPAT_RELAXATION telemetry.
- End-to-end test harness with 20+ test cases exercising edge cases (arrays, nested objects, optional/required interplay, legacy relaxations).

Non-goals: SDK autotransforms, UI for editing manifests (tracked separately in PM).

Rollout plan:
1) Merge authoring guide + initial validator behind a feature flag (canary projects).
2) Run linter on historical manifests and produce migration list. Notify manifest owners.
3) Enable permissive runtime validation for all projects with telemetry only.
4) Offer 'strict mode' opt-in for projects that want early enforcement.
5) After 8 weeks of telemetry and migrations, flip default to stricter linting for new manifests only.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Overly strict validator will break integrators. Mitigation: Start permissive, use explicit compat block to opt out, add clear migration guides.
- Risk: Error messages remain too technical. Mitigation: Iteratively refine messages with UX/PM feedback and ship localized examples.

Open questions:
- What subset of JSON Schema features do we forbid to keep the DSL compact? (Proposed: disallow regex-based 'pattern' and complex 'oneOf' without explicit 'discriminator'.)
- Should the runtime automatically attempt safe coercions (e.g., string->int) or only suggest them? (Proposed: perform only non-lossy coercions when compat declared.)

Next steps / To do:
- Design review with Platform and DX (scheduled 2025-03-05).
- Implement server validator prototype and unit tests (ENG).
- Linter integration and Confluence docs (PM + DevRel).
- Add console dashboard tile for top validation errors (Console team).

design_decisions: Favor a small DSL subset rather than full JSON Schema to reduce author confusion.
Expose a per-manifest 'compat' block to encode relaxations explicitly.
Return structured, machine-readable error codes plus a human-friendly example_fix string.
Only auto-coerce when a compat relaxation explicitly allows it or when the coercion is non-lossy.
Linter warnings do not block deploys; strict mode is opt-in initially.
implementation_notes: Add validator to runtime call entrypoint; keep implementation in runtime/validation to reduce cross-service coupling.
Ship a mapping table from DSL 'profiles' to runtime validators for performance reuse.
Instrument validation with telemetry_tag and include in per-request sampling for example payload capture.
Create a small compatibility module that reads 'compat' and exposes a deterministic set of relaxations.
test_plan: Unit tests covering E_PARAM_MISSING, E_TYPE_MISMATCH, E_EXTRA_FIELDS, E_COMPAT_RELAXATION, E_SCHEMA_AMBIGUOUS.
Integration tests with runtime call path using sample tool manifests and simulated client payloads.
Load test focusing on nested arrays to validate CPU overhead and memory pressure.
End-to-end canary with 3 internal projects for 2 weeks capturing telemetry and migration metrics.
rollout_plan: Feature-flagged merge; enable for internal canaries only.
Run linter across historical manifests and notify owners via email with migration suggestions.
Enable permissive runtime validation and collect telemetry for 30 days.
Offer strict-mode opt-in and monitor error reduction and support tickets.
